taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Vernonia baldwinii and recognizes infraspecific variation; Texas plants align with the broad-leaved western ironweed concept.
look_here_first: Tall robust ironweed with broader rough leaves and broad terminal arrays of purple discoid heads. Leaves are much broader than in V. lindheimeri.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis and Kerr are exact target-zone records. Williamson is documented but outside the project target-county list and is not counted.

approval_exception.reason: Correct stale PASS while preserving learner admission.

best_field_traits: broad ovate to lance-ovate rough leaves
broad flattened to irregular terminal arrays
purple discoid heads with no rays
morphology_keys.comparison_training: V. lindheimeri is much narrower-leaved with strongly revolute margins and densely woolly lower surfaces.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Broad leaves favor V. baldwinii; intermediate plants may be hybrid and should not be forced to a parent.

photo_note: Rights-cleared exact-species visual anchor has been selected and routed for physical import. Continue hunting the diagnostic macro roles listed in visual_learning.photo_diagram_needs; do not treat a habit image as completing the gallery.

visual_learning.learner_goal: Separate broad-leaved V. baldwinii from narrow revolute-leaved V. lindheimeri while recognizing that V. × guadalupensis can bridge the parents.

look_sequence.look_at: one mature mid-stem leaf in full view
look_sequence.question: Is the blade broadly ovate/lance-ovate or very narrow and linear?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Start with leaf proportion, not flower color. Photograph the whole blade with a consistent scale.

look_sequence.question: Are the margins relatively flatter or strongly rolled under (revolute)?
look_sequence.teaching_note: A side-lit edge view teaches this better than a flat overhead photo.

look_sequence.question: Where is the hairiness concentrated and how woolly is the underside?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use matched macros of the same leaf area on both surfaces; V. lindheimeri should provide the strong densely woolly-underneath contrast.

look_sequence.question: Does the overall plant fit the robust broad-leaved ironweed architecture?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use this as supporting context after the leaf characters, not as the sole separator.

look_sequence.question: Does the plant cleanly fit one parent, or does it bridge them?
look_sequence.teaching_note: If leaf width, margin roll and indumentum are intermediate, keep V. × guadalupensis open rather than forcing a parent.

same_frame_features: whole mature leaf at same scale
comparison_board.baldwinii_side: much broader ovate to lance-ovate leaf; lower surface hairy/tomentose
comparison_board.other_side: very narrow linear leaf; strongly revolute margins; lower surface densely woolly/sericeo-tomentose
comparison_board.best_visual_lock: same-scale leaf + edge profile + underside macro

comparison_board.other_side: accepted natural hybrid may be intermediate between the two parents
comparison_board.best_visual_lock: three-column parent–hybrid–parent comparison rather than a binary key

photo_diagram_needs.annotation: mark blade width and length axes; label broad-leaved parent endpoint
arrow to relatively flatter margin and contrast with strongly revolute V. lindheimeri

photo_diagram_needs.role: three-column V. baldwinii × V. guadalupensis V. lindheimeri comparison
photo_diagram_needs.annotation: align same-scale leaves and the same diagnostic regions across all three

photo_diagram_needs.role: whole flowering habit + terminal head array
photo_diagram_needs.annotation: show where comparison leaves were sampled from the plant
label disc florets and absence of ray florets as genus/family context, not the parent separator

avoid_overtrusting: head color or general ironweed gestalt
one intermediate leaf on a possible hybrid
range status as an identification character
